metadata.course: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships
metadata.attribution: Original scope and sequence authored for the Luminfest Learning Harness, dedicated to the public domain under CC0.
metadata.scope: Structure only: concept titles, unit order and prerequisite intent. No third-party curriculum text is reproduced, and no restricted source is ingested.
metadata.description: A full Algebra 1 course: algebraic expression language, linear equations and inequalities, linear functions and modelling, statistics and data, systems, functions, exponents and radicals, exponential functions, polynomials and factoring, quadratic functions and quadratic equations.

id_namespace.reason: Concept ids are global; the prefix keeps this course disjoint from the shipped courses that share concept titles.

supplements: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry (1e, CC BY 4.0)
textbook_alignment.link_only_note: OpenStax Algebra 1 reports CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and is carried as a link-only study reference: never stored or quoted.

Linear Systems: Systems of Inequalities and Feasible Regions

concepts.title: A General Order
concepts.summary: Take out the greatest common factor first, then count the terms to choose a pattern, and always check by multiplying back.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Absolute Value as Distance
concepts.summary: The absolute value of x is its distance from zero, so |x| = a with a > 0 has two solutions, x = a and x = -a.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Adding and Subtracting Polynomials
concepts.summary: Addition combines like terms, and subtraction distributes the minus sign to every term of the polynomial being subtracted.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Additive versus Multiplicative Change
concepts.summary: Linear change adds a constant amount per step while exponential change multiplies by a constant factor, so their tables differ immediately.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: And versus Or
concepts.summary: A conjunction requires both conditions at once, while a disjunction requires at least one, which changes the shape of the solution set.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Arithmetic Explicit Rule
concepts.summary: The rule a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d gives any term directly from its position, and the slope of the sequence is d.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Association
concepts.summary: A scatter plot shows the direction, strength and form of an association between two quantitative variables.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Average Rate of Change
concepts.summary: The average rate of change over an interval is the change in output divided by the change in input, which is the slope of the secant line.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Bias and Precision
concepts.summary: Question wording, sampling method and measurement error each distort a conclusion in a different way, so they are diagnosed separately.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Building a Linear Model
concepts.summary: A constant rate together with a starting value gives a model of the form y = mx + b, with units on both the rate and the start.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Building a Quadratic Model
concepts.summary: A constant second difference, or a context with a maximum or minimum, points to a quadratic rather than a linear model.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Building an Exponential Model
concepts.summary: An initial value together with a constant percent change gives a model of the form f(t) = a b^t, with b determined by the change per period.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Center and Spread
concepts.summary: The mean and median describe the centre of a distribution, while the range, interquartile range and standard deviation describe its spread.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Checking a Model Against the Context
concepts.summary: A solution is accepted only when it satisfies the equation and makes sense in the situation, including its sign and size.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Checking a System Solution
concepts.summary: A proposed solution is verified by substituting it into both original equations, because a graphing error can imitate a solution.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Choosing a Method
concepts.summary: Factoring is fastest when the factors are clean, square roots when there is no linear term, and the formula always works.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Classifying Polynomials
concepts.summary: Polynomials are named by degree and by number of terms, which tells you which operations and patterns apply.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Combining Like Terms
concepts.summary: Like terms carry identical variable factors, so only their coefficients add and the variable part is unchanged.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Common Difference
concepts.summary: An arithmetic sequence adds the same difference at each step, so it is a linear function whose domain is the term positions.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Common Ratio
concepts.summary: A geometric sequence multiplies by the same ratio at each step, which is exactly why its terms follow an exponential rule.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Comparing Long-Run Behaviour
concepts.summary: Over a long enough interval exponential growth overtakes any linear growth, which is why the two models answer different questions.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Compound Interest
concepts.summary: Compounding applies the growth factor repeatedly, so more compounding periods raise the effective rate without changing the nominal one.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Computing with Scientific Notation
concepts.summary: Multiplying or dividing separates the coefficients from the powers of ten, and the result is renormalised into scientific form.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Conditional Relative Frequency
concepts.summary: Dividing by a row or column total gives a conditional relative frequency, which compares groups of different sizes fairly.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Constant Rate of Change
concepts.summary: A relationship is linear exactly when equal changes in the input produce equal changes in the output.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Constant Second Differences
concepts.summary: A table of values is quadratic exactly when the second differences are constant, just as a linear table has constant first differences.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Constraints as Inequalities
concepts.summary: Phrases such as at most, at least and no more than set a boundary rather than an exact value, which is what makes the model an inequality.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Converting Between Forms
concepts.summary: Algebraic rearrangement moves one form into another without changing the line, so the form is chosen for what it reveals.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Correlation and Causation
concepts.summary: Correlation measures only the strength of a linear association, so a strong correlation by itself never establishes a cause.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Cube Roots
concepts.summary: A cube root of a number is the value whose cube is that number, and unlike a square root it exists for negative inputs too.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Degree and Leading Coefficient
concepts.summary: The degree of a polynomial is its highest exponent, and the leading coefficient belongs to that highest-degree term.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Dimensional Analysis
concepts.summary: Carrying units through a computation shows whether the result is the quantity the question asked for, and cancels units like factors.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Direct Proportion
concepts.summary: A relationship of the form y = kx passes through the origin, and k is both the unit rate and the constant ratio y/x.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Direction of Opening
concepts.summary: The sign of the leading coefficient decides whether the parabola opens upward with a minimum or downward with a maximum.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Displays and Shape
concepts.summary: Dot plots, histograms and box plots expose shape, including skew and outliers, which a single summary number can hide.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Distributing Before Solving
concepts.summary: Clearing parentheses first turns a multi-step equation into the two-step form already solved, and avoids dividing by an expression.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Dividing by a Monomial
concepts.summary: Each term of the polynomial is divided by the monomial separately, because a sum divided by a term distributes.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Domain
concepts.summary: The domain is the set of allowed inputs, restricted by the context, by division by zero and by even roots of negative numbers.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Doubling Time and Half-Life
concepts.summary: A fixed doubling time or half-life determines the base and the exponent, so the model can be written from that single time.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Estimating a Solution
concepts.summary: When the bases cannot be matched, a solution is estimated from a graph or a table and checked by substitution.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Evaluating and Graphing
concepts.summary: Evaluation selects the branch whose interval contains the input, and the graph draws each branch only on its own interval.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Evaluating and Interpreting
concepts.summary: Evaluating substitutes a value into the rule, while interpreting states what the resulting output means in the situation.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Factored Form
concepts.summary: Factored form displays the x-intercepts directly, and their midpoint gives the axis of symmetry.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Factoring by Grouping
concepts.summary: Grouping terms in pairs with a shared factor exposes a common binomial factor, which then factors out of the whole expression.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Factoring Completely
concepts.summary: A factorisation is complete only when no remaining factor can be factored further, which sometimes requires two passes.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Feasible Region
concepts.topic: Systems of Inequalities and Feasible Regions
concepts.summary: In a constraint model the overlap is the set of allowed choices, and its vertices are where a linear objective reaches its extremes.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Finding an Inverse
concepts.summary: Swap x and y in the equation and solve for y; the result is a function only when the original passes the horizontal line test.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Finding Intercepts
concepts.summary: An intercept is where a graph meets an axis: set the other variable to zero and solve for the remaining one.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Formulas in Context
concepts.summary: A rearranged formula answers a different question about the same relationship, such as solving d = rt for the time t.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Fraction and Decimal Fluency
concepts.summary: Common denominators, reciprocals and decimal place value are the arithmetic moves every later algebraic step still depends on.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Fractional Exponents
concepts.summary: A rational exponent combines a power and a root, so a raised to m/n is the nth root of a to the m.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Fractions and Decimals in Equations
concepts.summary: Multiplying by the least common denominator or by a power of ten clears fractions and decimals without changing the solution set.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Geometric Explicit Rule
concepts.summary: The rule a_n = a_1 r^(n-1) gives any term from its position, and r is the base of the matching exponential function.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Graph Features
concepts.summary: An exponential graph has a horizontal asymptote, passes through (0, a), and grows or decays without ever crossing the asymptote.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Grouping and Order of Operations
concepts.summary: Exponents first, then multiplication and division left to right, then addition and subtraction, with grouping symbols overriding the order.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Growth and Decay Factors
concepts.summary: A base greater than one grows, a base between zero and one decays, and the percent change is the base minus one.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Half-Planes
concepts.summary: A linear inequality in two variables has a boundary line and one of the two half-planes it divides the coordinate plane into.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Horizontal and Vertical Lines
concepts.summary: A horizontal line has slope zero because its output never changes, and a vertical line has undefined slope because its input never changes.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Identities and Contradictions
concepts.summary: An equation that reduces to a true statement holds for every value, while one that reduces to a false statement has no solution.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Infinitely Many Solutions
concepts.summary: Coincident lines are the same equation written twice, so every point on the line solves the system.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Intercepts in Context
concepts.summary: In a model an intercept usually marks a starting amount, a break-even point or a time when a quantity reaches zero.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Interpreting a Boundary
concepts.summary: The solution set states every allowed value, and a boundary value is tested separately because the context may or may not include it.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Interpreting a Unit Rate
concepts.summary: A unit rate restates a ratio as per one, which makes comparisons and scaling direct and keeps the units attached.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Interpreting and Evaluating a Model
concepts.summary: A model is used by substituting an input for a prediction, and every output is judged against the range the context allows.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Interpreting Vertex and Intercepts
concepts.summary: In a model the vertex is the optimum value and the intercepts are where the modelled quantity is zero.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Intersection as Solution
concepts.summary: A solution of a system is an ordered pair that satisfies both equations at once, which is exactly a point where the two graphs meet.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Interval Notation
concepts.summary: A parenthesis excludes an endpoint and a bracket includes it, and an interval is always read from left to right.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Inverse Operations
concepts.summary: An equation stays true when the same operation is applied to both sides, so the inverse operation isolates the variable.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Irrational Numbers
concepts.summary: An irrational number cannot be written as a ratio of integers, so its decimal neither terminates nor repeats.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Joint and Marginal Frequencies
concepts.summary: A two-way table counts pairs of categories, and its margins give the totals for each variable on its own.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Key Features
concepts.summary: Intercepts, intervals of increase and decrease, and local maxima and minima summarise what a function graph is doing.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Leading Coefficient One
concepts.summary: For a trinomial with leading coefficient one, two numbers whose product is the constant and whose sum is the middle coefficient give the factors.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Leading Coefficient Other Than One
concepts.summary: Splitting the middle term into two terms whose product is the product of the end coefficients allows factoring by grouping.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Less Than and Greater Than Forms
concepts.summary: An inequality of the form |x| < a gives one interval between -a and a, while |x| > a gives two rays pointing outward.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Line of Best Fit
concepts.summary: A trend line summarises an association and supports prediction inside the observed range, not far outside it.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Linear versus Nonlinear
concepts.summary: A table whose successive differences change, or a graph that curves, is not linear no matter how straight a short segment looks.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Making a Perfect Square
concepts.summary: Adding the square of half the linear coefficient turns a quadratic into a perfect square, which then yields to the square root property.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Modelling with Quadratics
concepts.summary: A context about maximum height, area or an optimum yields a quadratic equation whose solutions are interpreted and checked in the situation.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Moving Between Forms
concepts.summary: Radical form and rational-exponent form describe the same quantity, and each one makes a different simplification visible.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Multi-Step Inequalities
concepts.summary: The solving steps match linear equations; only the direction rule for negative factors differs, and endpoints are open or closed by symbol.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Multiplying Polynomials
concepts.summary: Every term of one factor multiplies every term of the other, and like terms are combined afterwards.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Negative and Rational Inputs
concepts.summary: Parentheses around a substituted negative protect its sign, which is why (-3)^2 and -3^2 are different quantities.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Negative Exponents
concepts.summary: A negative exponent means the reciprocal of the positive power, so a negative exponent never makes the value negative.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: No Solution
concepts.summary: Parallel lines never intersect, so a system describing them is inconsistent and has no solution.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: One-Step Equations
concepts.summary: A single inverse operation undoes the one operation attached to the variable, whether it is addition, subtraction, multiplication or division.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Operations with Signed Numbers
concepts.summary: Adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing signed numbers follows sign rules that keep arithmetic consistent with the number line.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Ordered Pairs and Quadrants
concepts.summary: A point (x, y) is located by a horizontal and a vertical displacement, and the axes divide the plane into four quadrants.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Overlapping Regions
concepts.topic: Systems of Inequalities and Feasible Regions
concepts.summary: The solution of a system of inequalities is the overlap of the individual solution regions, so a point must satisfy every inequality.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Parallel Lines
concepts.summary: Parallel lines have equal slopes and never meet, because equal slopes mean equal rates of change with a fixed vertical offset.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Perfect-Square Trinomials
concepts.summary: A trinomial whose first and last terms are squares and whose middle term is twice the product factors as a binomial squared.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Perpendicular Lines
concepts.summary: Perpendicular slopes are negative reciprocals, so their product is -1 and one line rises where the other falls.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Piecewise Notation
concepts.summary: A piecewise function applies different rules on different intervals of its domain, with each interval stated beside its rule.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Point-Slope Form
concepts.summary: The form y - y1 = m(x - x1) writes the line through a known point with a known slope, which is the form a context usually supplies.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Power Rules
concepts.summary: A power of a power multiplies exponents, and a power of a product applies the exponent to every factor.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Precision and Reasonable Answers
concepts.summary: A result carries the precision of its inputs, so an answer is checked against the size and units the context implies.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Probability Rules
concepts.summary: Probabilities lie between zero and one, complementary events sum to one, and the addition rule handles events that can overlap.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Product and Quotient Properties
concepts.summary: The product property of radicals lets a perfect-square factor leave the radical, which is what simplifying a radical means.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Product and Quotient Rules
concepts.summary: Multiplying powers of one base adds the exponents, and dividing subtracts them, because the factors are counted rather than multiplied.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Quadratic versus Linear
concepts.summary: A quadratic graph curves with a single turning point, while a line has the same rate of change everywhere.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Random Sampling
concepts.summary: A random sample supports inference about the population, while a sample chosen for convenience does not.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Range
concepts.summary: The range is the set of outputs a function actually produces, which is not always every number the rule could theoretically give.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Rational Numbers
concepts.summary: A rational number is a ratio of two integers, and its decimal expansion either terminates or repeats.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Rationalising a Denominator
concepts.summary: Multiplying by a form of one removes a radical from a denominator without changing the value of the expression.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Reading a Graph
concepts.summary: A graph is read by tracing an input to its output, noting intercepts, where the graph rises or falls, and where it is steepest.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Reading f(x)
concepts.summary: The notation f(x) names the output of the function f at input x, so f(3) means the output when the input is three.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Rearranging a Formula
concepts.summary: Solving for a named variable treats the other variables as constants and applies the same inverse operations in reverse order.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Recursive Definition
concepts.summary: A recursive rule states the first term and how each later term follows from the previous one, which is enough to generate the whole sequence.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Residuals
concepts.summary: A residual is the actual value minus the predicted value, and a pattern in the residuals shows the line is missing structure.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Reversing the Symbol
concepts.summary: Multiplying or dividing both sides by a negative number reverses the inequality because the number line is reflected.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Sample Space and Events
concepts.summary: The sample space lists every possible outcome, and an event is a subset of that space whose probability is a fraction of the whole.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Sequence as Function
concepts.summary: A sequence is a function whose domain is the positive integers, so its graph is a set of isolated points rather than a curve.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Shifts, Stretches and Reflections
concepts.summary: Changing the horizontal and vertical shift moves the vertex, while changing the leading coefficient stretches or reflects the parabola.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Slope in Context
concepts.summary: The units of a slope are output units per input unit, so in a model it names the rate the situation actually describes.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Slope-Intercept Form
concepts.summary: The form y = mx + b displays the slope m and the y-intercept b directly, which is why it is the fastest form to graph from.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Solution Sets on a Number Line
concepts.summary: An inequality has a set of solutions described by a symbol, a number-line graph or interval notation, rather than a single value.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Solving Absolute Value Equations
concepts.summary: Isolate the absolute value first, then split into the positive and negative cases and reject any solution that fails the original equation.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Solving and Graphing
concepts.summary: Isolate the absolute value, rewrite it as a compound inequality, then graph the result and check both endpoints.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Solving by Matching Bases
concepts.summary: If two powers of the same base are equal then their exponents are equal, so rewriting both sides with one base solves the equation.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Standard Form of a Line
concepts.summary: The form Ax + By = C describes the same line, and its intercepts are read by setting each variable to zero in turn.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Standard Form of a Parabola
concepts.summary: Standard form shows the y-intercept immediately and, with the vertex formula, locates the turning point.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Substitution and Order of Operations
concepts.summary: Evaluating replaces each variable with a value and then applies the order of operations, so the same expression always produces one value.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Sum and Difference of Cubes
concepts.summary: A sum or difference of cubes factors into a binomial and a trinomial whose signs follow a fixed pattern.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Terms, Coefficients, and Constants
concepts.summary: A term is a product of a number and variables; its coefficient is that number, and a constant term contains no variable at all.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Testing a Point
concepts.summary: Substituting a test point decides which side of the boundary satisfies the inequality, and a dashed boundary excludes the line itself.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Testing Equivalence
concepts.summary: Two expressions are equivalent when every substitution gives the same value, and simplifying one into the other proves it structurally.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: The Difference of Squares
concepts.summary: The product of a sum and a difference collapses to the difference of the two squares because the middle terms cancel.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: The Discriminant
concepts.summary: The discriminant decides the number of real solutions: positive gives two, zero gives one, and negative gives none.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: The Distributive Property
concepts.summary: a(b + c) = ab + ac lets a factor outside parentheses multiply every term inside, which is the move that removes grouping.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: The Elimination Method
concepts.summary: Adding or subtracting multiples of the equations removes a variable when its coefficients become opposites or equal.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: The Exponential Growth Pattern
concepts.summary: A function of the form f(x) = a b^x multiplies by b at each unit step, so equal input steps give equal output ratios rather than equal differences.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: The Function Definition
concepts.summary: A function assigns exactly one output to each input, so a relation that gives one input two different outputs is not a function.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: The Greatest Common Factor
concepts.summary: The greatest common factor of all terms moves outside the parentheses by the distributive property, which is always the first factoring step.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: The Inverse Relationship
concepts.summary: An inverse swaps the roles of input and output, so it undoes whatever the original function did.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: The Number of Real Solutions
concepts.summary: A parabola meets the x-axis zero, one or two times, and that count matches the number of real solutions of the equation.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: The Parent Graph
concepts.summary: The graph of y = |x| is V-shaped with its vertex at the origin and slopes of 1 and -1 on its two branches.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: The Principal Square Root
concepts.summary: The principal square root is the nonnegative number whose square is the radicand, which is why solving x^2 = a gives both signs.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: The Quadratic Formula
concepts.summary: The formula solves every quadratic in standard form, and it is derived by completing the square on the general equation.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: The Slope Formula
concepts.summary: Slope is the change in y divided by the change in x between two points, so it measures steepness and direction together.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: The Square of a Binomial
concepts.summary: Squaring a binomial gives the square of the first term plus twice the product plus the square of the last term.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: The Square Root Property
concepts.summary: If x squared equals a nonnegative number then x is plus or minus the square root of that number, because both signs square to the same value.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: The Substitution Method
concepts.summary: Solving one equation for a variable and substituting into the other turns a system of two equations into one equation in one variable.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: The Vertical Line Test
concepts.summary: A graph represents a function exactly when no vertical line meets it more than once, which is the graphical form of the definition.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: The Zero Exponent
concepts.summary: Any nonzero base raised to the zero power is 1, because dividing equal powers leaves no factor behind.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: The Zero Product Property
concepts.summary: If a product equals zero then at least one factor is zero, so factored form turns a quadratic equation into two linear equations.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Transformations of the Absolute Value Graph
concepts.summary: Shifts move the vertex, a stretch changes how steep the branches are, and a reflection turns the V upside down.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Translating a Context into an Equation
concepts.summary: Define the unknown, state the relationship in words, then write the relationship symbolically with units attached to each quantity.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Translating Words into Expressions
concepts.summary: A phrase such as five more than twice a number becomes 2x + 5, one operation at a time, with order words deciding the grouping.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Two Constraints
concepts.summary: Two conditions on two unknowns form a system whose solution satisfies both conditions simultaneously, not one after the other.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Two-Step Equations
concepts.summary: Undo addition or subtraction first and multiplication or division second, which reverses the order the expression was built in.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Two-Way Tables and Probability
concepts.summary: Joint, marginal and conditional probabilities are read directly from a two-way table by choosing the right denominator.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Units and Unit Conversion
concepts.summary: Multiplying by a conversion factor equal to one changes the unit without changing the quantity, so 12 inches and 1 foot name the same length.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Variables and Expressions
concepts.summary: A variable names a quantity that can change, and an expression combines variables, numbers and operations without an equals sign.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Variables on Both Sides
concepts.summary: Collecting variable terms on one side and constants on the other reduces the equation to a single coefficient times the variable.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Vertex and Axis of Symmetry
concepts.summary: The vertex is the turning point of a parabola, and the axis of symmetry is the vertical line through it that mirrors one side onto the other.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Vertex Form
concepts.summary: Vertex form displays the vertex and the direction and steepness of the opening in one glance.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Writing Scientific Notation
concepts.summary: A number in scientific notation is written as a factor between 1 and 10 times a power of ten, which fixes both size and precision.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships

concepts.title: Zeros and x-Intercepts
concepts.summary: A zero of a quadratic function is an input whose output is zero, which is exactly where its graph meets the x-axis.

provenance.source: Algebra 1 - Expressions, Linear and Quadratic Relationships
